title: Smooth ambient coordinates adapted to a free cotangent restriction
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ and residue field $k$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $X$ be an $R$-scheme locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $Y\hookrightarrow X_k$ a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $U\subseteq Y$ be open and smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose the restriction $\Omega^1_{X/R}|_U$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback] is locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of structure sheaves. For every $u\in U$ there is an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq X$ containing $u$ with $W=Y\cap V\subseteq U$, a smooth affine finite-type $R$-scheme $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$, a closed $R$-immersion $V\hookrightarrow Z$, and functions $y_1,\ldots,y_r,z_1,\ldots,z_n\in C$ such that, writing $H=\ker(C\to D)$ and $J=\ker(C\to\mathcal O_W(W))$, one has $H\subseteq J=(\pi,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. The coordinate morphism $Z\to\mathbf A^{r+n}_R$ given by these functions is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. The module $\Omega_{C/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is free with basis $dy_1,\ldots,dy_r,dz_1,\ldots,dz_n$, and the canonical map
$$\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C C/J\longrightarrow\Omega_{D/R}\otimes_D C/J$$
is an isomorphism. Moreover $C$ is Noetherian (every ideal is finitely generated). No generic smoothness, flatness of $X$, density of sections, or group structure is assumed.

Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Fix $u\in U$. Since $Y$ is closed in $X$ and $Y\setminus U$ is closed in $Y$, choose an affine finite-type neighbourhood $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}D$ of $u$ disjoint from $Y\setminus U$. Shrink it further so that, with $W_0=Y\cap V_0=\operatorname{Spec}E$, $\Omega_{D/R}\otimes_DE$ is free of constant rank $q$. This is exactly the assumed local freeness, interpreted by [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Write $E=D/I$; $\pi\in I$ because $W_0$ lies in the special fibre. Choose finitely many algebra generators of $D$ and the resulting surjection $P=R[T_1,\ldots,T_N]\twoheadrightarrow D$, with kernel $K$. Its spectrum is the initial closed embedding. Subsequent shrinking of an affine scheme will always be to a principal open containing $u$; the inverse image in $V_0$ is then a principal affine open as well.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $P\twoheadrightarrow D$ and tensor the resulting right exact sequence with $\kappa(u)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], its middle term is $\kappa(u)^N$ and its last term has dimension $q$. Therefore the vectors $dh$ for $h\in K$ span a kernel of dimension $c=N-q$. Select $h_1,\ldots,h_c\in K$ whose differential vectors are a basis of this kernel. Select $c$ rows giving a nonzero square minor, and reorder the variables so they are the first $c$. Let $\Delta=\det(\partial h_j/\partial T_i)_{1\leq i,j\leq c}$. Then $\Delta(u)\ne0$. For $c=0$ use the empty list and $\Delta=1$.

Set $B=P/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$ and $C_0=B[1/\Delta]$. Replace $D$ by $D[1/\Delta]$ and $E$ by its corresponding localization. Since every $h_j$ belongs to $K$, there is still a surjection $C_0\twoheadrightarrow D$. The presentation $C_0=R[T_1,\ldots,T_N,t]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c,t\Delta-1)$ is standard smooth: use the pivot variables $T_1,\ldots,T_c,t$. Its determinant is $\Delta^2$, since the upper-right block is zero and the last diagonal entry is $\Delta$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] show that $\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ is smooth over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{C_0/R}$ is free on the remaining $q=N-c$ variable differentials.

The canonical map $\Omega_{C_0/R}\otimes_{C_0}E\to\Omega_{D/R}\otimes_DE$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. Both modules are free of rank $q$. Choose bases. At $u$ its matrix is a surjective square matrix over $\kappa(u)$, so its determinant is nonzero. Invert a lift of that determinant from $E$ to $C_0$. The adjugate formula gives an inverse on all of the resulting $W_0$. Rename the localized rings $C_0,D,E$. Their differential modules have the claimed localizations by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization]. In particular the canonical restricted differential map is now an isomorphism, not merely an isomorphism on one residue fibre.

Every principal localization of our standard smooth presentation is again standard smooth: to invert an element represented by $g$, append a variable $s$ and the equation $sg-1$, and append $s$ to the pivot variables. The new determinant is the old determinant times $g$, a unit. Thus all the preceding principal shrinkings preserve standard smoothness. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-base-change] the special fibre $Z_{0,k}=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/\pi C_0)$ is standard smooth over $k$, and [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] make it smooth over $k$. The closed subscheme $W_0$ is smooth over $k$ by the hypothesis $W_0\subset U$.

Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] to $W_0\hookrightarrow Z_{0,k}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. It gives, near $u$, an etale chart with coordinate functions $\bar y_1,\ldots,\bar y_r,\bar z_1,\ldots,\bar z_n$, whose last coordinates cut out $W_0$ scheme-theoretically. Choose a principal affine neighbourhood of $u$ contained in the chart, and lift its defining denominator to $C_0$. Localize $C_0,D,E$ accordingly. The chart functions now belong to $C_0/\pi C_0$. Lift them to functions $y_i,z_j\in C_0$. If $J_0=\ker(C_0\to E)$, the coordinate-subspace assertion gives $J_0/\pi C_0=(\bar z_1,\ldots,\bar z_n)$, so $J_0=(\pi,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. The chosen $z_j$ belong to $J_0$ since their images in $E$ are zero.

source.place: Tag 0FUE (lemma-etale-local-structure), applied over k to the closed smooth pair; affine restriction and lifting modulo pi.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-etale-localization-relative-differentials], applied to this etale chart and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], the differentials $d\bar y_i,d\bar z_j$ are a basis of $\Omega_{(C_0/\pi C_0)/k}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], this module is $\Omega_{C_0/R}\otimes_{C_0}(C_0/\pi C_0)$ with exactly these lifted differential vectors. Since $\Omega_{C_0/R}$ is free of rank $q$, reducing at $u$ shows $r+n=q$. The matrix of $dy_i,dz_j$ in its existing basis has determinant nonzero at $u$. Invert this determinant. Its adjugate supplies an inverse matrix, so $dy_i,dz_j$ form a basis of $\Omega_{C_0/R}$ on the resulting affine neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 04BX (lemma-sheaf-differentials-etale-localization), Tags 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring) and 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change); determinant lifting as in BLR 3.3 Proposition 5.

proof.text: Consider $g=(y_i,z_j):\operatorname{Spec}C_0\to\mathbf A^{r+n}_R$. Its source is smooth by the standard smooth construction and its target is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], the relative differential map for $g$ sends the coordinate basis to the basis $dy_i,dz_j$. Therefore [lem-sfb-smooth-morphism-cotangent-isomorphism-etale] supplies an open neighbourhood of $u$ on which $g$ is etale. Choose a principal affine neighbourhood inside it and denote its ring by $C$. Its inverse image in $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is the final $V$, with ring again denoted $D$. Restriction preserves the coordinate differential basis and the isomorphism along $W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization].

source.place: BLR 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed pp.68-69 (PDF pp.74-75), first two construction paragraphs; online primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $E=\mathcal O_W(W)$ for the final $W=Y\cap V$. The final surjections $C\twoheadrightarrow D\twoheadrightarrow E$ give $H=\ker(C\to D)\subseteq J=\ker(C\to E)$. The equality $J=(\pi,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ persists under each localization: an element maps to zero after localization precisely when a power of the inverted element times a numerator maps to zero before localization. The isomorphism of restricted differential modules established in step 4 and preserved in steps 6--8 is the canonical map in the statement, because on every generator it is $dc\otimes e\mapsto d(c|_D)\otimes e$. All localizations were made at elements nonzero at $u$, so $u\in V$ and $W\subset U$.

proof.text: The ring $R$ is Noetherian: by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] every ideal is principal. The ring $C$ is finite type over $R$, since it was obtained from a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables by finitely many principal localizations (each inverse is one additional algebra generator). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. The construction worked at the arbitrary chosen $u$ and used no flatness of $X$, smoothness of its generic fibre, density condition, or group law.
